newsitem.title: INDIA: Four killed in militant attacks in northeast India.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in militant attacks in northeast India.

text.p: Four people were killed in India's rebellious northeastern region in scattered incidents of violence coinciding with independence day celebrations, police said on Friday.
Separatist guerrillas shot the four people dead in three overnight attacks in Assam state, police in the region's biggest city, Guwahati, told Reuters.
Separatist militants blew up a bridge in the central section of the state and set on fire a small railway station on the main track connecting the region with the rest of India, they said.
Authorities clamped tight security on a ceremony in Guwahati commemorating India's 50 years of independence, deploying soldiers and paramilitary troopers on rooftops across the city.
Residents were not allowed to open their doors or windows until the event, which went off peacefully, ended and dignitaries had left the site of the flag-raising.
On Thursday, seven people were killed and eight injured when a bomb planted by suspected separatists exploded on a train track in northeastern India, derailing a passenger carriage.
It was the latest attack in a mounting campaign of insurgency-related violence in the northeastern region, where dozens of separatist groups are fighting Indian rule.
